judgments.title: SIM SWEE HARN & ors v LIM SEONG KEN
judgments.catchwords: 1. The late Sim Bee Tuan (“the Deceased”) was, by all accounts, a well-known eu char koay seller. The later years of his life, however, were marked by declining health and personal hardship, during which he took up residence in a temple, where he came to be under the care of those who managed its affairs. 2. Against that backdrop, the present dispute over his estate arises. By a will now impugned, the Deceased bequeathed the entirety of his estate to the Defendant, who was at the material time a caretaker and manager of the said temple, to the complete exclusion of his immediate family. The Plaintiffs, being the children and issue of the Deceased, have commenced these proceedings to challenge the validity of that will. 3. The stakes for the parties are considerable. If the impugned will is upheld, the Defendant stands to inherit the whole of the Deceased’s estate, leaving nothing for the Plaintiffs. Conversely, if the will is found to be invalid, the estate will fall to be distributed in accordance with the rules of intestacy, under which the Plaintiffs stand to benefit. 4. It therefore falls upon this Court to determine the validity of the impugned will. That determination must be made by careful reference to the evidence adduced and the applicable principles of law, to which this Court now turns.
judgments.judge: YA Dr Choong Yeow Choy

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya v AFIF AIMAN BIN ABDUL RAZAK
judgments.catchwords: CRIMINAL LAW – Sexual offences against children – Physical sexual assault – Touching or physical contact with child of a sexual nature – Elements of offence under s. 14(a) Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 – Whether touching or physical contact with child established – Whether touching or contact sexual in nature having regard to part of body touched and nature and extent of contact – Whether victim a "child" within meaning of s. 2(1) Act 792 – Explanation 1 to s. 14 Act 792 (touching by any part of body, object, or through clothing) – Explanation 2 to s. 14 Act 792 (factors relevant to determining sexual nature of touching) CRIMINAL PROCEDURE – Acquittal and discharge at close of prosecution's case – Prima facie case under s. 173(f) Criminal Procedure Code – Principles under s. 180 CPC applied equally to trial under s. 173 – Maximum evaluation of prosecution evidence – Whether prosecution failed to establish a prima facie case – Whether trial court entitled to acquit and discharge accused without calling for defence – Appeal by Public Prosecutor against order of acquittal – Standard of appellate intervention in criminal appeals – "Plainly wrong" test – Whether appellate court may disturb trial court's findings of fact absent the audio-visual advantage enjoyed by trial court – Whether appellate court confined to determining whether findings on credibility were supported by evidence or vitiated by misdirection in law – Function of appellate court not to substitute its own assessment of witnesses for that of trial court EVIDENCE – Child witness – Competency to give unsworn evidence – s. 133A Evidence Act 1950 – Distinction between competency and credibility of child witness – Whether finding of competency precludes subsequent adverse finding on credibility – Credibility, consistency and reliability of child witness's testimony – Whether child's account substantially guided, influenced, or mediated by parent – Whether narrative of alleged offence originated from child herself or was supplied by another witness – Chronology and circumstances in which child's complaint first emerged – "Unusually convincing" standard for evidence of a child where conviction would rest substantially thereon – s. 18 Act 792 – Dispensation of requirement of corroboration for evidence of a child – Whether court's duty to test quality of child's evidence survives dispensation of corroboration requirement – Weight to be accorded to isolated discrepancies versus discrepancies going to source of narrative – Absence of independent corroborating demonstration of alleged act – Medical evidence – Conflicting expert medical opinion between examining physicians – Approach to resolving conflicting expert evidence by examining process of examination and analysis undertaken by each expert – Evidential value of medical report recording history as attributed to third party rather than direct account from victim – Whether medical evidence conclusive of commission of sexual assault – Non-production of video recording of child interview centre interview – Whether failure to tender recording fatal to prosecution's case or gives rise to adverse inference – Discretion of prosecution as to conduct of its case and manner of adducing witness evidence under s. 5 Evidence Act 1950

judgments.title: SIVACHANDRAN A/L S JAYARAJAH v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Constitutional Law - Federal Constitution - Articles 5(1), 8(1) and 8(2) Fundamental liberties - Life and personal liberty - Human dignity - Equal protection of the law - Whether it is in violation of medical ethics for medical officer to be participate in the execution of whipping. Judicial whipping - Corporal punishment - Whether judicial whipping amounts to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment (“CIDT”) - Whether punishment of whipping is inconsistent with constitutional protection of life, dignity and bodily integrity. Whether whipping is disproportionate and therefore contrary to Article 8(1) - Whether exemption of women from whipping constitutes prohibited discrimination on ground only of gender is contrary to Art 8(2) - Intelligible differentia. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.
